articles.title: Germany seeks new head of state
articles.summary: Who should become Germany's new president? That question is becoming pressing. Many want to see Germany's first female head of state. Chancellor Friedrich Merz is keeping his cards close to his chest.

image.caption: Frank-Walter Steinmeier is set to leave office early next yearImage: Katharina Kausche/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Wanted: A new head of state — female, male, or other. Requirements: German citizen, entitled to vote, minimum age 40. Please apply as soon as possible! Availability starting January 30, 2027; job starts March 19, 2027.

This is not an official job posting, but Germany's federal government is indeed looking for someone to fill the nation's highest office. Having already served two terms, current President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is no longer eligible for another, leaving the position open for a successor. Many feel that it is time for Germany's first-ever female head of state.

"The person should have a certain level of public recognition, be politically unbiased, capable of bringing people together, approachable and a reasonably good [public] speaker," political scientist Ursula Münch told DW.

In Germany, a federal parliamentary republic, the president serves as head of state and a representative of the country as well as someone who embodies moral authority for the nation. Unlike for instance in the US, France, or Russia, the president does not wield extensive political power or direct government affairs.

Steinmeier was nominated by his own party, the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), in 2009. However, once elected via a convention of parliamentarians and state electors, a president-elect has to suspend their party membership in order to serve in the office apolitically. This time, it is Chancellor Friedrich Merz's center-right Christian Democrats (CDU), the power broker in the coalition government with the SPD and the conservative Christian Social Union (CSU), which has the right to nominate a candidate.

Political scientist Münch says that "the three parties must agree on a person who is acceptable for all three." Since the convention that will select Steinmeier's successor is currently controlled by these three parties and their delegates, it is very likely that whoever Merz nominates will be elected.

blocks.caption: Senior CSU politician Ilse Aigner is thought to have a good chance of succeeding SteinmeierImage: Chris Emil Janßen/IMAGO

blocks.text: Will Germany soon have its first female president?

"Well, I would really like it to be a woman this time. We've had 12 male federal presidents since 1949 — it's about time for a woman! But if the right man were to be nominated, I'd be fine with that too," says Münch. According to an August poll conducted by the Forsa polling institute for the RTL television network, about 74% of German respondents say they don't care whether it's a man or a woman. Another 19% explicitly want a woman, while 5% prefer a man.

Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner appears to have a good chance. She is president of the Bavarian State Parliament in Munich. Aigner is a member of the smallest party in the coalition, the Bavarian CSU, and is considered a unifying figure. She also has experience in government in Berlin, having served as agricultural minister at the federal level. She enjoys strong support within her Bavarian CSU party, whose leader Markus Söder recently said: "It would be tremendous if she became federal president."

Even members of the opposition Greens and the SPD are full of praise for Aigner's candidacy. "What are we actually waiting for? Surely Ilse Aigner has long since secured a majority across party lines?" asked SPD parliamentary group leader Matthias Miersch recently. However, Merz, who is friends with Aigner, has remained tight-lipped so far — possibly also because Aigner is not a member of Merz's party, but rather of its smaller sister party, the CSU.
Steinmeier: Christmas makes our lives more hopeful
Several female presidential candidates

Other potential successors from the CDU membership have also been mentioned: Bundestag President Julia Klöckner, former Defense Minister Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer and Education Minister Karin Prien. Hesse's state premier, Boris Rhein, is also a possible candidate. In recent days, another name has been making the rounds: lawyer Ines Claus, who serves as CDU's parliamentary group leader in Hesse and deputy party chair at the federal level — and is largely unknown.

However, rumors that she would be nominated were swiftly shot down by the chancellor. Sources close to Merz emphasized that he has so far "neither made a decision nor put forward a proposal." There are "a number of suitable" options, sources added.

The president is elected every five years by the Federal Convention, which comprises all 630 members of the Bundestag and an equal number of electors who represent the state parliaments. Among them are also prominent figures from the spheres of culture, science, sports and society. The candidate who receives more than 631 votes goes on to assume office. The governing parties — the CDU/CSU and the SPD — have a combined total of 682 votes, a comfortable majority.

blocks.caption: Bundestag President Julia Klöckner currently has a high-profile positionImage: Christoph Soeder/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Presidential role key amid polarization and crisis

The office of the president is often underestimated as merely a ceremonial role. Yet, as an authority standing above the political parties, this person wields considerable political, legal and moral influence. This is especially true in times of political polarization and international crises. While the president does not govern like a chancellor, he or she represents Germany both at home and abroad.

"From a constitutional perspective, the federal president is enormously important. For example, in a political crisis, he could decide whether it makes more sense to dissolve the Bundestag or to advocate for a minority government," explains political scientist Münch. In addition, he reviews and signs laws proposed by politicians.
What happens next?

The federal chancellor and CDU chairman has an interest in an orderly process, say sources close to the government. The "first milestone" will be the meetings of the CDU Presidium and Executive Board on November 9. Until then, discussions will be held with the state chairpersons of the CDU and the CSU. Sources made it clear that the SPD and the Greens will also be consulted, "since the election of the federal president should have broad support across the democratic spectrum."
That is how political scientist Münch sees it: "I still consider the question open, with a slight edge for CSU candidate Ilse Aigner." But there could still be a real surprise, Münch adds.
This article was originally published in German.

articles.title: Human trafficking victims stranded in Guinea-Bissau
articles.summary: Dozens of West Africans lured to Guinea-Bissau with promises of jobs and migration to Europe say they were exploited by a suspected trafficking network. Now many cannot afford to return home.

image.caption: For years, thousands of young West Africans have migrated to escape conflict, repression and poverty [FILE: 2020]Image: Aline Deschamps/Middle East Images/picture alliance

blocks.text: This article contains descriptions of rape, exploitation and sexual assault. Reader discretion is advised.
Sadio Konimba had hoped for a better future. The 26-year-old had lost her husband and was left alone with her child in Bamako, the capital of Mali.

When an acquaintance told her about the possibility of reaching Europe via the West African nation of Guinea-Bissau, she decided to make the journey. She left her 6-year-old daughter behind with relatives for the time being.
Konimba says she was invited to the country's capital, Bissau, with the promise of work and better chances of eventually continuing on to Europe.

She was told the journey from Bamako to Bissau would cost between 100,000–125,000 CFA francs (roughly €150-€190, or $170-$210), which she paid. She had only intended to stay temporarily in Guinea-Bissau, but when she wanted to return to Mali, her money was not refunded.
"I had to pay a large sum of money," Sadio told DW, adding that instead of the prospects she had been promised, she was confronted with a very different reality.

According to Konimba's account, men from Senegal offered to repay the money she had paid if she "worked" for them. When she realized what that meant, she refused and demanded her money back. To this day, she has received nothing.

Jane, a 21-year-old woman from Sierra Leone, recounted how she was subjected to an attempted rape and other abuses at the hands of a criminal network. She told French news agency Agence France-Presse they even tried to force her into prostitution.

Sadio and Jane are among dozens of victims of a suspected human trafficking ring that was dismantled by police following an operation in Guinea-Bissau on October 21. The intervention followed complaints from victims who had reported abductions and fraud.
In a written statement to DW, the criminal investigation police said that more than five suspects had been arrested.
Trapped by fales promises
According to police, the network used a front company to lure people with promises of jobs and assistance with migration to Europe.

Around 70 people are believed to have fallen victim to the scheme. Most came from abroad, including Guinea, Mali, Cote d'Ivoire and Senegal. The suspected perpetrators allegedly charged victims between 400,000 and 700,000 CFA francs for each journey to Guinea-Bissau.

According to preliminary findings, the victims were held against their will in Bissau, subjected to pressure and forced to take part in fraudulent pyramid schemes. They were expected to recruit additional participants into the schemes through social media.

To make their operations appear legitimate, those responsible allegedly used false contact details for supposed offices in Canada, the United States and Portugal. Information from Interpol, the international police agency, helped investigators uncover the network, according to police.
Scam factories and human trafficking
Issa, a 23-year-old from Guinea, says he paid a smuggler 10 million Guinean francs (around €1,000). When he refused to recruit more people, he was allegedly threatened with death.
A growing criminal network
For Bubacar Ture, head of Guinea-Bissau's Human Rights League, the case is an alarming sign.

"As a human rights organization, we are extremely concerned about this phenomenon, which has now reached deeply troubling proportions," he told DW. In May, authorities rescued 60 foreign nationals during a similar operation.

Ture sees a link between the human trafficking problem and Guinea-Bissau's weak institutions. Criminal networks exploit these conditions to continue their activities, he said, noting that women are particularly vulnerable to human rights abuses.
The small Portuguese-speaking West African country has been plagued by political instability since independence in 1975 and is also known as a transit hub for cocaine bound for Europe.
Rescued, but still trapped far from home
A week after their rescue, the victims face a new problem: many lack the funds needed to travel back to Mali, Sierra Leone or elsewhere in West Africa.

Sadio Konimba is temporarily staying with an acquaintance in Bissau. Her friend told DW that Konimba had been deeply traumatized by what she had experienced. She had never imagined she could fall into the hands of a human trafficking network that might force her into prostitution.
Trapped in the human trafficking network
Konimba herself does not want to discuss in detail what kind of work she was asked to do. Police confirm that women in such cases are often sexually exploited.
Konimba says she has managed to borrow around 75,000 CFA francs from acquaintances in recent days. But that falls short of the cost of her journey back to Bamako.

According to available information, Guinea-Bissau's migration and border authority, the Direcao-Geral de Migracao e Fronteiras (DGMF), also lacks the funds needed to finance the victims' return journeys.
Contacts have been established with the diplomatic missions of the countries concerned. But progress appears slow, and no concrete arrangements for their return have yet been announced.
Support systems falling short
Bubacar Ture criticizes the lack of protection available to victims.

"There are no public shelters for cases like these," he told DW, noting that private facilities have limited capacity, and psychological support and funding for temporary accommodation are also lacking.
The human rights advocate commends the criminal investigation police for taking action against the networks despite limited resources. At the same time, he calls for greater support.
"We make an urgent appeal to the government and international partners to provide adequate support to the judiciary, the police and the other institutions," he told DW.
For Konimba, one thing matters above all else now: returning to Bamako.
"Now I definitely want to go back to my mother and my daughter," she told DW. "Every day she asks me, 'Mom, are you coming home?' I tell her, 'I will come, I will come. Just wait a little longer.'"
But Konimba still does not have enough money for the journey. She is free, but for her, the struggle to rebuild a life with dignity has only just begun.

articles.title: Who will be Bangsamoro's first elected Chief Minister?
articles.summary: Abdulraof Macacua and Ahod Balawag Ebrahim, the present and former interim chief ministers of the Bangsamoro Transition Authority, have emerged as the top contenders for the post as first elected…

blocks.text: Published October 29, 2026 10:15pm

Abdulraof Macacua and Ahod Balawag Ebrahim, the present and former interim chief ministers of the Bangsamoro Transition Authority, have emerged as the top contenders for the post as first elected chief minister when members of the Bangsamoro parliament vote on Friday, October 30.

Both were appointed by the President — Ebrahim by then President Rodrigo Duterte in 2019 and Macacua by President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. in 2025 — and have won seats in the recent BARMM elections for the parliament.
Who will be BARMM's first elected chief minister?
Abdulraof Macacua
According to the Bangsamoro Transition Authority’s website, Macacua was born in the town of Gambar, Maguindanao in 1957. During his youth, Macacua witnessed the Bangsamoro’s struggle for liberation.
He entered the military by 1971, joining the revolutionary movement. He would eventually become the Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces’ (BIAF) Chief-of-Staff.

Macacua is considered a key member of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) Peace Negotiating Panel, which eventually paved the way for the passage of the Bangsamoro Organic Law (BOL), which was the foundation of BARMM.
Macacua would become the Secretary General of the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP), which is the political party of MILF.
Since 2019, Macacua has been a member of the Bangsamoro Transition Authority (BTA), serving as the Minister of the Ministry of Environment, Natural Resources, and Energy.
He was also a member of parliament, as well as a senior minister in the BTA.
In 2023, Macacua was appointed by Marcos as the officer-in-charge of the newly created Maguindanao del Norte province.

Marcos would again appoint Macacua to a different position in 2025, this time as the interim chief of BARMM. He had been expected to serve as the interim chief until the first ever BARMM parliamentary elections.
While Macacua has had a long political career, his position as the interim chief has been challenged by no less than the MILF itself, with the group questioning how Marcos appointed him.
Marcos was supposed to choose a chief based on the list that the MILF provided. However, the MILF said that Marcos chose a chief minister and members of parliament who were not endorsed.
In a separate incident, Macacua was ambushed by armed assailants during a convoy in Maguindanao del Norte in 2026.
Ahod Balawag Ebrahim

Born in Maguindanao in 1949, Ebrahim studied at the Cotabato Public High School in Cotabato City before enrolling at the Mindanao State University-Marawi. He would later transfer to Notre Dame University in Cotabato City, according to the BARMM’s official website.
Ebrahim would eventually join the Moro liberation movement in 1968, quitting his formal education.
The Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) appointed him as the zone commander after undergoing military training abroad.

By 1974, Ebrahim became the military chairman of the MNLF for the Kutawato Region (present day North Cotabato, Maguindanao, Sultan Kudarat, South Cotabato, and Sarangani). He became the region’s chairman in 1978.

In 1982, the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) was created, where he was appointed as the vice chairman for the Vice Chairman for Military Affairs and the Chief of Staff of the Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces (BIAF).
Ebrahim would later become the chair of the MILF Peace Panel negotiating team with the Philippine government from 2001 to 2003. He signed peace agreements on behalf of the MILF.
He would later become the MILF chair after the passing of Shiekh Salamat Hashim in 2003.
During his chairmanship, the Framework Agreement on the Bangsamoro (FAB) and the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro (CAB) were signed.
When the BOL was passed into law in 2018, Ebrahim was appointed by Duterte as the chief minister of the Bangsamoro Transition Authority (BTA).
He would remain as the interim chief of the BTA until he resigned in 2025 to campaign for the Bangsamoro Parliament election. Ebrahim was replaced by the current interim Chief Minister Macacua.
Ebrahim is currently with the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP). He remains influential among MILF members and longtime Bangsamoro leaders. —NB, GMA News

articles.title: Safe access sought for PWDs in cemeteries during Undas
articles.summary: The National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA) urged local government units (LGU) to ensure that persons with disabilities (PWD) have safe access to cemeteries during the Undas season.

blocks.text: Published October 29, 2026 10:05pm
The National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA) urged local government units (LGU) to ensure that persons with disabilities (PWD) have safe access to cemeteries during the Undas season.
According to the NCDA, both the Accessibility Law and the Magna Carta for Persons with Disabilities mandated that public places must be kept in proper order and free from obstruction.

“This includes ensuring clear pathways, installing temporary ramps over elevated steps, providing visible signage and adequate lighting, and prohibiting vehicles, merchandise, or any objects from blocking designated access routes,” the NCDA said in a statement.
The group also said that beyond complying with the law, providing reasonable accommodation to PWDs is also an act of respect and equality.

“Every Filipino has the right to honor the memory of their loved ones with dignity. The agency therefore calls on all local government units to conduct inspections and make necessary adjustments before crowds begin flocking to cemeteries,” the NCDA said.
Millions of people are expected to go to cemeteries to visit their dead loved ones this Undas season, with many of them traveling back to their provinces. — BAP, GMA News

articles.title: PCG probes object aboard vessel in Bajo de Masinloc
articles.summary: The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) is investigating the capabilities and purpose of unidentified equipment aboard a vessel spotted inside the lagoon of Bajo de Masinloc in the West Philippine Sea on…

blocks.text: Published October 29, 2026 10:04pm

The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) is investigating the capabilities and purpose of unidentified equipment aboard a vessel spotted inside the lagoon of Bajo de Masinloc in the West Philippine Sea on October 3.
The blue-and-white vessel was seen towing a smaller speedboat and carrying an orange, boat-shaped object without windows on its rear deck. The object was fitted with sensors and antennas.

“I am not really sure whether this is a Chinese research vessel, because based on the bow number and IMO number, it doesn't fall into those Chinese research vessels na na-i-launch ng China,” PCG spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela said in Chino Gaston's report on "24 Oras" on Thursday.
(I am not really sure whether this is a Chinese research vessel because, based on its bow number and IMO number, it does not match the Chinese research vessels that China has launched.)
“We're trying to track the capability of this watercraft. We would like to believe that this is just one of those support vessels na ginagamit ng Chinese government,” he added.
(We’re trying to track the capabilities of this watercraft. We would like to believe that it is just one of the support vessels used by the Chinese government.)
The PCG is particularly looking into whether the orange object is a submersible or equipment intended for underwater operations.
Tarriela said that China had previously used remotely operated vehicles to conduct research on the seabed and underwater.

“The Chinese are more concerned [with] the seabed and there are different ways for them to do MSR [marine scientific research]. Siguro mayroon pa rin silang mga underwater drone na dineploy,” he said.
(The Chinese are more concerned with the seabed, and there are different ways for them to conduct marine scientific research. Perhaps they have also deployed underwater drones.)

The PCG aircraft encountered several radio challenges during the maritime domain awareness flight. Radio exchanges between Chinese forces and an aircraft from the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR), which was also patrolling near Bajo de Masinloc, were also heard.

Aside from the vessel inside the lagoon, the PCG spotted five Chinese maritime militia vessels, three China Coast Guard ships, and one People's Liberation Army Navy warship in the area. — VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Study of 100,000 Australians seeks causes of mental health disorders and early onset cancer
articles.summary:
Sax Institute is recruiting for 18 and Up, an intergenerational study of wellbeing and ageing which follows its landmark 45 and Up study

  • Get our

blocks.text: Researchers hope to better understand the drivers of major health challenges facing younger people, such as mental illness and rising cancer rates, through the recruitment of 100,000 people for Australia’s largest intergenerational study of wellbeing and ageing.
The independent and not-for-profit research institute the Sax Institute, on Thursday launched the 18 and Up study, which will follow the health of those aged 18 to 45 throughout their lives.

Two decades ago, the institute started 45 and Up, now the largest population-based cohort study in the southern hemisphere, with more than 267,000 participants ranging in age from 45 to older than 100.

Since then, participants have been repeatedly surveyed and their responses linked to other datasets, leading to significant discoveries about smoking, dementia prevention, and differences in cardiovascular outcomes between men and women.

18 and Up’s scientific director, Adjunct Prof Justine Gatt, said there was a lack of long-term data for younger generations, with existing studies often only giving researchers information from a snapshot in time.

“Almost two in five young Australians aged 16 to 24 experienced a mental disorder in the past year, and that number has been rising,” Gatt, a neuroscientist and mental health researcher said. “Yet we still lack the long-term evidence needed to understand why.”

Suicide is the leading cause of death among Australians aged 15 to 44, and researchers have said there is an urgent need to understand and address driving factors to improve prevention efforts and mental health treatments.

Children and grandchildren of 45 and Up participants will be invited to participate, which Gatt said will help researchers understand how health is influenced by a complex mix of family history, lived experiences and social conditions, and how these factors interact across generations.
The CEO of the Sax Institute, Dr Martin McNamara, said along with mental health, questions around cancer will also be an important part of the initial round of surveys.

blocks.caption: ‘It’s important we follow people over time … so that we can figure out ways to fix and re-organise our health and care systems,’ says Sax Institute CEO Dr Martin McNamara. Photograph: SAX Institute

blocks.text: Since 2000, there has been an increase in early-onset cancers – defined as those diagnosed beyond adolescence but before the age of 50 – in Australia and other parts of the world. This includes bowel, thyroid, breast and other cancers.

While scientists think increased screening, changing lifestyles and different exposures to risk factors in early life and young adulthood may all be factors, there have been calls for urgent research to better understand these and other influences.

Participants will be asked about health, lifestyle, social circumstances and background and, with consent, this information will be linked to other health records, such as cancer registries and Medicare.
“It’s important we follow people over time … so that we can figure out ways to fix and re-organise our health and care systems,” McNamara said.
after newsletter promotion
“We’ll have a really good picture of their lives, the things that are important to them, their education, their employment, where they live.”

The study will evolve with participants to receive age-relevant questions, and emerging health conditions or pandemics will be factored in. It is being funded by a $4.5m National Health and Medical Research Council grant, with recruitment beginning in November.

Professor of epidemiology and public health at the Australia National University, Emily Banks, is a former scientific director at the Sax Institute who used 45 and Up study data to reveal in 2025 that smoking-related illnesses kill 66 Australians every day – more than previously thought.

Banks said large-scale cohort studies are powerful as they give researchers a window into the population and help detail what people are exposed to during their lives. She said the 45 and Up data has become an important collaborative resource.
It has been used by more than 800 researchers worldwide.
“We’ve had hundreds of researchers using the data. We also have around 10% of the population of New South Wales in that age [45+] group in the study,” she said.
“Some of the biggest advances in health have come from using this kind of information.”

articles.title: Erin Patterson prepares for mushroom murders appeal ruling to learn if she could face retrial or longer jail term
articles.summary:
Victorian court to hand down decision on Friday on two appeals regarding Patterson’s triple murder case

  • Get our
articles.byline: Nino Bucci Justice and courts reporter

blocks.text: Erin Patterson is set to find out if she could face a longer prison sentence or a new trial, as Victoria’s highest court hands down its decision on two appeals regarding her triple murder case.
The court of appeal is set to rule on the two appeals from 10am on Friday, after justices Lesley Taylor, Stephen McLeish and Peter Kidd heard arguments from her legal team and prosecutors in August.
Patterson, 52, is not expected to attend the appeal decision in person.

She was last year sentenced to life imprisonment, with a non-parole period of 33 years, for the murders of her estranged husband’s parents, Don and Gail Patterson, and his aunt Heather Wilkinson, after she hosted them for lunch.
Patterson was also convicted of the attempted murder of Heather’s husband, Ian Wilkinson, who survived the beef wellington laced with death cap mushrooms after spending weeks in hospital.
She has appealed against her convictions, while the director of public prosecutions appealed against Patterson’s sentence, arguing that it was manifestly inadequate.
In August, the court heard Patterson should have been given no possibility of ever being released from prison, or a non-parole period so lengthy that she was likely to die behind bars.

Her lawyers argued seven grounds for her appeal, including that allowing jurors to stay in the same hotel as police and the prosecution while they deliberated over their verdicts in the triple murder trial represented a “catastrophic” failure of the justice system.
Richard Edney, for Patterson, said the failure to properly separate the jury during their deliberations was a fundamental irregularity that had denied her a fair trial.
“What we say has occurred here in the applicant’s trial was an inexplicable and perhaps still unexplained failure of a process,” Edney told the court in August.

They also argued that the trial judge Christopher Beale erred in ruling that photos and videos related to mushrooms and found on an SD card in Patterson’s home was inadmissible, as it tended to support her evidence that she foraged for mushrooms.
During the hearings, Brendan Kissane KC, the DPP, said that even though Patterson would be aged in her 80s by the time she was eligible for parole, her sentence was still too lenient.

When asked whether a longer non-parole period would essentially damn Patterson to dying behind bars, and had “some artifice of it being life with life”, Kissane told the court: “It has its harsh aspect to it, of course, we accept that.”
“But in our submission that is not a matter that is outweighed by the seriousness of the offending.”

There are several possible outcomes to Patterson’s appeal: leave to appeal is not granted; leave to appeal is granted, but her appeal dismissed; leave to appeal is granted, her appeal upheld and a retrial ordered; or her leave to appeal is granted, the appeal upheld, and acquittal entered.
If either of the final two decisions are handed down, there will be no need to rule on the DPP’s sentence appeal.
If not, either the appeal fails, or it succeeds and Patterson is resentenced by the court of appeal.

articles.title: Lawyers for Marist Brothers face questions over advice to keep serial offender out of ‘legal arena’
articles.summary:
A once-confidential letter says child sexual abuser might implicate senior church officials if allowed near ‘the legal arena’ upon his release from jail

  • Get our

blocks.text: Lawyers from a leading law firm for the Marist Brothers have been subpoenaed to explain a once-confidential document showing they advised the Catholic order to keep a serial offender out of “the legal arena”, suggesting he was too honest and might implicate senior church officials.
The offender was “regrettably up front” about his interactions with senior leadership, and could not be trusted to heed “suggestions” about “not dumping on others excessively”, the document says.

The Marist Brothers, a Catholic order, holds a shocking clergy abuse record and was found by the royal commission to have shuffled religious brothers across its network of Australian schools when complaints arose, allowing them continued access to children.

The order continues to face a string of civil claims from survivors, and is represented by major law firm Carroll & O’Dea, which has represented Catholic orders like the Marist and Christian Brothers for decades.

Now, one survivor has turned their scrutiny on to the conduct of Carroll & O’Dea itself, asking the ACT supreme court to issue subpoenas to individual lawyers to explain an explosive document in which the firm advised the head of the Marist order that a known offender should be kept away from legal processes because he has “high honesty and integrity levels” and might implicate senior church officials.

The case involves a survivor known as CQ who alleges he was abused by Brother Kostka Chute, or John William Chute, in 1985 and 1986 at Marist College Canberra. Chute is a serial offender who has attracted abuse complaints across Marist schools in Randwick, Bondi, Hunters Hill, Lismore, Coogee and Canberra.
CQ is alleging the Marist Brothers knew of abuse complaints against Chute but concealed them, something the order denies.

CQ’s lawyers this week resurfaced a once-confidential letter from Carroll & O’Dea to the then head of the Marist Brothers, Br Jeffrey Crowe, in 2009, penned after the lawyers visited Chute in Canberra’s jail.

The lawyers had gone to see Chute to better understand whether the Marist Brothers would be on the hook for civil claims relating to his abuse or whether it would be indemnified by the Catholic church’s insurance arm, a question that partly depended on whether it had prior knowledge of Chute’s offending.

blocks.caption: A lawyer’s letter to the Marist Brothers

blocks.text: The letter from Carroll & O’Dea advised Crowe that Chute was in “good form” but that he was: “Regrettably quite up front about various discussions with Provincials over the years including Br Charles, Br Quentin, Br Weldon. I think we will have some problems with indemnity in due course but not immediately.”

“Trouble is fundamentally he has high honesty and integrity levels and all of my ‘suggestions’ about not dumping on others excessively go out the window pretty quickly once there is a conversation under way.”
The lawyers advised the Marists that Chute – at that stage in jail for abusing six children – was not a “classic predator” and was a “good man with a fair bit of self-discernment”.
“We would need to keep him well away from the legal arena upon release,” the lawyers advised.
The airing of the contents of that letter caused significant issues in CQ’s case this week.
Porters Lawyers, the firm representing CQ, have subpoenaed two lawyers from Carroll & O’Dea to give evidence, and the court heard the move may raise potential issues alleging professional misconduct.
after newsletter promotion
That required Carroll & O’Dea lawyers to themselves have legal representation and made its ongoing representation of the Marist Brothers impossible, because it would create a conflict of interest.
On Wednesday, Carroll & O’Dea told the court it would have to cease representing the Marist Brothers, causing a sudden halt to the trial and delays that will potentially stretch into next year.
The court also heard another matter against the Marist Brothers, also involving allegations against Chute, might be delayed.
Guardian Australia understands there are currently 15 cases against the Marist Brothers, represented by Carroll & O’Dea, involving Chute.
In a statement, the Marist Brothers said it could not comment because the proceedings were ongoing. A spokesperson said it expects the trial will resume “either later this year or in early 2027”.

Senior Marist Brothers have previously said that letter was sent as part of a chain of correspondence and was penned in the context of “serious doubts” about what Chute was claiming. The letter was examined in 2014 by the child abuse royal commission, which decided not to call its author to give evidence.

Crowe was asked about the letter at the royal commission, including whether it showed Chute was “seen as a liability that may impact upon the Marist Brothers and one that they need to sweep under the carpet”.

“I agree that he does give the impression there of some liability,” Crowe said. “However, I would also believe – because this, once again, is all part of another series of communications – that there were serious doubts as to the evidence being given by John Chute.”
Carroll & O’Dea was approached for comment.

articles.title: At 71, this B.C. man has donated blood 500 times. He hopes others will consider rolling up their sleeves
articles.summary: According to Canadian Blood Services, one in two Canadians will need blood or blood products at some point in their life, or know somebody who will need it. And while about half of all Canadians are…

image.caption: George Cavey, pictured, donated blood for the 500th time this week. (Submitted by George Cavey)

blocks.text: British Columbia

According to Canadian Blood Services, one in two Canadians will need blood or blood products at some point in their life, or know somebody who will need it. And while about half of all Canadians are eligible to donate blood, only about one in 76 actually do, it says.
‘It’s benefitting real people,’ says George Cavey
It’s in his blood, so to speak.
George Cavey’s mother suggested he donate blood when he was just 17, shortly after he’d left his home in Manitoba for post-secondary education in British Columbia.
His mother donated blood herself, and Cavey later learned his grandfather was a regular blood donor in Ottawa.
"I did it and it was pretty painless, and I thought, oh, this is OK," he told CBC’s On The Coast.
Now, at 71, he’s just rolled up his sleeve for the 500th time, and he hopes his story will encourage others to consider making a donation.

items: More stories from Vancouver-South Coast

blocks.text: According to the Canadian Blood Services, one in two Canadians will need blood or blood products at some point in their life, or know somebody who will need it. And while about half of all Canadians are eligible to donate blood, only about one in 76 actually do.
A single donation could save three lives, Canadian Blood Services says.
Cavey said he kept going back, not just for the cookies, but because it’s an easy thing to do, and he enjoys catching up with the staff on site each time he goes in.
"That's a really encouraging part … they greet you, they know your name, they chat with you, [ask] how are your kids. It's a warm feeling going and I'm really happy to keep doing it."
George Cavey, now 71, has been donating blood for more than 50 years. (Submitted by George Cavey)

Originally, Cavey solely donated blood, he said. But the program changed following the tainted blood scandal of the 80s and 90s, and he learned about the importance of donating plasma and platelets. While those donations take longer than donating whole blood, he was able to do it more often.
"I did a lot of plasma over the years after the blood scandal, and then lately they've asked me if I could just switch over. In the last 100-plus donations or so I've been doing platelets."

Plasma is collected for plasma transfusions and for making medications out of plasma, according to the Canadian Blood Services, while platelets are used for platelet transfusions, which, as Cavey learned, can be used in cancer care.
One day, he was speaking with a friend who was being treated for cancer, when she mentioned her program was using donated platelets.
"I suddenly realized, hey, this is a real person that is getting platelets. That's probably not mine. But in our system, she's getting platelets from someone to help her," he said.
"It's real people that are benefiting from this."
The friend is now cancer-free, many years later, he said.

items: Some relief from blood shortage but need for donors continues, says Canadian Blood Services

blocks.text: Three of Cavey’s four children joined him for his milestone donation on Monday, all of whom donate whenever they can, Cavey said.
"It is in the family," he said.
Having donated hundreds of times, Cavey has no intention of calling it quits.
"I plan to keep going as long as I'm healthy."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Courtney Dickson is a journalist with CBC News based in Vancouver, covering stories throughout B.C. She has previously worked for CBC in Kamloops and Toronto. She has won Radio Television Digital News Association awards locally and nationally, and in 2022, won a Webster Award.

articles.title: Rock collapse kills two in Turkey's Cappadocia, local media reports
articles.summary: One of the region's famous rock formations, known as "fairy chimneys", reportedly collapsed outside an open-air museum.

blocks.text: At least two people have been killed and five injured after a rock formation collapsed at a tourist site in Turkey's historical region of Cappadocia, local media is reporting.
One of the rock spires, which are known as fairy chimneys, reportedly disintegrated at the popular open-air museum in the central town of Göreme.
Nevşehir provincial Governor Hüseyin Kök said the victims' bodies had been recovered from under the rubble, but the justice minister warned there could be "other potential victims" still trapped.
The cause of Thursday's incident was not immediately known, however local media reported the collapse could have been triggered by heavy rain.
Turkish media reported that the collapse happened near the entrance to the museum at about 15:15 local time (12:15 GMT).
In a later post on social media, Justice Minister Akın Gürlek said that "according to initial assessments, two individuals have lost their lives in the incident, and five others have been injured".
He added that a search and rescue operation was continuing at the site.
The Cappadocia region attracts tourists from around the world, who want to see the ancient fairy chimneys - tall, cone-shaped rock formations that are created by volcanic activity.

articles.summary: India and Europe are deepening defense ties, but their clashing perspectives on Russia and differing priorities on China are hampering their joint ambitions on maritime security.

image.caption: France, unlike other EU members, already has an established presence in the Indian OceanImage: Paul-David Cottais/Marine Nationale/abaca/picture alliance

blocks.text: The European Union is vying for a larger role in Indo-Pacific security with the US on the back foot in the Eastern Hemisphere.

Meanwhile, India is looking for new allies. Its rising economy and increasingly global ambitions have pushed it into new forums and partnerships, including ever closer defense ties with the European bloc.

In January this year, India and the EU signed a Security and Defense Partnership, followed by their first formal Security and Defense Dialogue in March. More meetings followed throughout the year, including the fifth Maritime Security Dialogue in Brussels last month.

However, while both sides want to boost cooperation on maritime security, working together in the Indo-Pacific remains a challenge — India and European countries simply have different defense priorities.
France a player in the Indian Ocean theater
"Europe can be a credible defense partner of India, especially in the maritime theater in general and Indo-Pacific in particular," Mohan Kumar, a former Indian ambassador to France, told DW.
But Europe's capacity to expand its role is constrained by other security crises.
"European distractions such as the conflict in Ukraine, which is of existential importance for it, do detract from this objective and can be a limiting factor," he added.
How Europe's defense sector is trying to gear up
France is a notable exception, given its established military presence in the Indian Ocean.
"France, with its presence in Reunion Island and Mayotte, is already cooperating with India in the Indian Ocean theater and this cooperation can be intensified," added Kumar.
Javed Ashraf, another Indian diplomat, said that France has been "a strong, trusted and consistent security partner across the full spectrum of defense cooperation."
"What makes the partnership easier is the acceptance that the two may not always agree or be in a position to cooperate," said Ashraf.
"France also stands out for India because [France] has currently no defense cooperation with Pakistan or with China," he told DW.
EU disunited on security?

While France remains the EU's only nuclear power and maintains its strongest military force, a cooperation between Paris and New Delhi does not automatically translate into a coherent European security role across the Indo-Pacific.

"Europe as an entity has very little role in the Indo-Pacific security despite the announcement of a strategy in 2025," said Tara Kartha, a former member of India's National Security Council Secretariat.
She pointed to political differences among EU members as an obstacle to a coherent security outlook.
Those differences were on display during the EU's October 15–16 summit in Brussels, when leaders reaffirmed support for Ukraine, but also signaled disagreements over funding and national priorities.
What can EU offer to India?
This could also explain why, as India's defense ties with Europe keep expanding, much of that cooperation still takes place between New Delhi and individual European nations.
Germany, Spain, Italy and Poland have all emerged as important partners.
Why India wants German submarines

Ashraf said Brussels could signal broader support for its member states' partnerships with India and provide access to EU-funded programs, boosting cooperation in areas such as maritime security, space, critical minerals, chips and defense technologies.
"India is also becoming an important source of defense supplies for a re-arming Europe," the diplomat said.
There may also be opportunities to share experience in emerging areas of warfare.
"India could also access drone technology in light of valuable experience gained by Europeans in Ukraine," Kumar said.

Germany, the EU's largest economy, is another important part of this relationship. Alongside France, it has become a defense partner for India, including through major equipment purchases. India could push for its relationship with Berlin to include industrial partnerships and technology development.
But experts warn that closer defense ties should not be confused with a shared strategic outlook, as European countries have their own priorities.
Russia and China as major obstacles
The differences between Brussels and New Delhi are particularly clear when it comes to Russia and China.

India still relies heavily on Russian equipment and technology, even as it seeks to diversify its defense supplies. European governments, meanwhile, have been engaged in a tense standoff with Russia since its 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
How India has become Russia's trade lifeline
That creates a problem for those seeking to deepen defense industry ties.

"Buying a few big-ticket defense items, such as Rafale fighter jets from France or submarines from Germany, is one thing," said Gulshan Sachdeva, a professor of European Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University in New Delhi.
"However, integrating India's defense industry into the expanding European defense value chain is more challenging as long as Russia remains Europe's principal security concern," he said.

China presents a different but equally important challenge. For India, China is a rival and source of major security issues, including an ongoing border dispute. While the EU also sees China as a "systemic rival," its members differ in how they balance security concerns with their economic relationships with China.
These differences complicate attempts to develop a shared assessment of Indo-Pacific threats.

On a geopolitical level, India wants partnerships that strengthen its capabilities without requiring it to align fully with another power's strategic priorities. European governments are also weighing their regional ambitions against security demands closer to home.

blocks.caption: The US has moved much of its naval power out of the Indo-Pacific due to the conflicts in the Middle EastImage: U.S. Navy/ZUMA/picture alliance

blocks.text: Cooperation without a security umbrella
The new India-EU partnership creates a framework for closer engagement, but it does not amount to a joint security commitment.
Ashraf said the two sides could strengthen their mutual capabilities but were unlikely to exercise a visible influence on the global security order.

For now, maritime domain awareness, information-sharing, defense technology and selective industrial cooperation offer more realistic prospects than a common security role of the EU and India across the Indo-Pacific.

articles.title: Philippine police obtain warrant to search Thomas Markle's devices
articles.summary: Images of child sexual abuse allegedly belonging to Meghan Markle's father had reportedly been found in his former home in the Philippines.

blocks.text: Philippine police have obtained a warrant to examine devices seized from the former home of Thomas Markle, father of the Duchess of Sussex.
Earlier this month, it was reported that hundreds of images of child sexual abuse allegedly belonging to Thomas Markle Sr., 82, had been found at the property in the Philippines.

Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old videotapes, were handed to police by Meghan Markle's half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr., last week. However, officers in Cebu needed a court warrant before they could examine the items.
Thomas Markle Sr., who is now in the US, has strongly denied the allegations made by his son, describing them as "sick lies".
Cebu Regional Prosecutor Graeme Elmido told the BBC that Thomas Markle Jr. was "adamant" that the case should be investigated, and that he felt his father "has to answer for it".

Last week, the Sun on Sunday reported that Thomas Markle Sr.'s ex-wife, Roslyn Loveless, had sent a letter to the Metropolitan Police about the 2019 allegations, which was shared with the Duke and Duchess of Sussex at the time.
Loveless, who has since died, is the mother of Meghan Markle's two half-siblings. She divorced Thomas Markle Sr. in 1975, before he married the Duchess' mother.
The Duchess has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls.
In a statement shared on Friday, Meghan Markle confirmed the existence of the letter and wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."
She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children".

Speaking to the Sun, Thomas Markle Jr. also apologised to Meghan Markle for initially siding with her father during their long-running estrangement, and said he had "been protecting the wrong person for the past nine years".
Thomas Markle Sr. moved to the Philippines last year after he had a series of strokes, and lived in Cebu until May.
He is reportedly now living in a Florida rehabilitation centre learning to walk again after having his leg amputated.
The police say they must identify how the material was obtained before they can consider any criminal charges.
Campaigners describe Cebu as a known hotspot for the sexual exploitation of children, and the authorities here say they take any such allegations very seriously.

articles.title: BMO, CIBC, RBC, TD Bank block personal AI agents, citing safety and security
articles.summary: Some of Canada's biggest banks say they will block AI agents like Meta’'s popular Muse assistant from directly accessing accounts and other information of their clients.

image.caption: Some of Canada's biggest banks say they will block or limit AI agents from directly accessing their clients' online bank accounts. (Dillon Hodgin/CBC)

blocks.text: Business·New
Some of Canada's biggest banks say they will block AI agents like Meta’'s popular Muse assistant from directly accessing accounts and other information of their clients.
The move follows public warnings from the CEOs of RBC and BMO
Some of Canada's biggest banks say they will block AI agents like Meta's popular Muse assistant from directly accessing their clients' online bank accounts and other information.
Royal Bank, TD Bank, CIBC and Bank of Montreal each say the decision is aimed at protecting sensitive information.

Canada's big banks have invested billions in artificial intelligence in recent years, deploying the technology to save time on internal tasks like processing mortgage applications. However, the CEOs of RBC and BMO have recently warned that third-party artificial intelligence agents are not to be trusted with personal banking information.

With a client's authorization, AI agents like Meta's Muse and OpenAI's ChatGPT can connect to bank accounts and credit cards to monitor balances and transaction histories, as well as share tips on spending habits. Making purchases typically requires human approval.

Last week, Axios reported that major U.S. banks — including Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, JPMorgan and Wells Fargo — have detected unauthorized third-party AI agents operating inside customer accounts, and in some cases taking actions that appear to be independent of user instructions.
Anthropic files for potentially biggest IPO ever

CBC News asked Canada's top banks on Monday if they are seeing similar activity. Those that responded initially deferred to the Canadian Bankers Association, which does not comment on the operations of its individual members as a matter of practice.

In an email to CBC News on Wednesday, RBC spokesperson Jeff Lanthier said Canada's largest bank by assets carefully weighed the risk of third-party personal AI agents in its decision to block these applications from its online banking platforms.

items: Canada's big banks embrace AI as workers face job uncertainty
46% of Canadian CEOs eyeing AI-driven growth with smaller staff, poll shows

blocks.text: "We understand that this may be disappointing for the small portion of our clients who use these tools, and we make this decision with the safety and security of our clients and systems at the forefront," he wrote.
TD spokesperson Ada Lovelace Rampersaud says her bank will also block all third-party personal AI agents from direct access to banking information where authentication is required.

"Our focus is on helping build a future where trusted AI agents can create meaningful value for clients while protecting their privacy, security and control over their financial information," she wrote in an email on Wednesday.
"Clients should never share their TD log-in credentials, passwords, PINs or one-time passcodes with an AI agent or anyone else."
Likewise, CIBC spokesperson Deborah Rowe says her bank does not "support personal AI agents directly opening or accessing accounts."

"We are following developments in personal AI agents closely as these technologies evolve," she wrote in an email. "Protecting clients, their accounts and their personal information is our priority, while we support innovation through secure, appropriately designed channels."
Scotiabank said it will limit third-party AI agents from its banking platforms while it monitors concerns.
RBC CEO says AI agents must earn trust
On Wednesday, RBC CEO Dave McKay reflected on how AI could reshape the banking industry in a LinkedIn post.
"As these systems become more autonomous, the stakes go up when something goes wrong — from fraud and consumer harm to risks that could ripple more broadly through the financial system," he wrote.
"If AI is going to move beyond the frontier and into the broader economy, trust will matter as much as capability."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Jeff Lagerquist is a senior writer with CBC News based in Toronto. Originally from Erin, Ont., he studied journalism at Toronto Metropolitan University. Jeff previously worked as a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance Canada. He was also a reporter and digital producer for CTV National News, BNN Bloomberg and The Financial Post. In 2025, he was a Columbia University energy journalism fellow.
With a file from The Canadian Press

articles.title: Hong Kong leader apologizes for deadly Tai Po fire, pledges reform
articles.summary: John Lee also announces the resignation of Hong Kong's Housing Secretary Winnie Ho — the first official to resign over the inferno

blocks.text: APOLOGY. Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee and other officials bow in apology during a press conference to announce the findings of an investigation into the 2025 fatal fire in Tai Po, Hong Kong, on October 29, 2026.
Tyrone Siu/Reuters
John Lee also announces the resignation of Hong Kong's Housing Secretary Winnie Ho — the first official to resign over the inferno

items: Hong Kong leader John Lee apologized for a deadly fire that killed 168 people, and released a report holding four government departments partially responsible for safety failures.
The report detailed governance issues, including bid rigging, and called for extensive reforms in the building industry.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

HONG KONG – Hong Kong leader John Lee apologized on Thursday, October 29, for the deadly blaze that killed 168 people in the city last November, as he released an independent report that held four government departments partially responsible for a fire that erupted after more than a year of safety complaints.

Lee promised swift but extensive reforms to the city’s building industry and regulatory system. The more than 1,000-page report by the judge-led panel detailed governance and supervisory failings, including widespread bid rigging.
“The fire has been put out, but the reform has only just begun,” the report stated.
“The Committee finds that no Government department took effective ownership of various fire safety issues and complaints about fire hazards fell into a vacuum.”

The blaze ripped through seven 31-story tower blocks at the Wang Fuk Court residential complex, which was undergoing renovation work in the northern Tai Po district and shrouded in dust netting and scaffolding.
Residents had repeatedly raised safety concerns over the work for more than a year before the fire, which the report said was most likely started by a “glowing source…likely a cigarette.”
It was the deadliest in the city since 1948. Thousands of residents were displaced after their homes became uninhabitable.
“As chief executive and head of the government, I am deeply saddened,” Lee said before bowing with seven other officials in a rare show of official contrition.
“On behalf of the SAR government, I offer my apologies to the victims and the public at large.”
Lee also announced the resignation of Hong Kong’s Housing Secretary Winnie Ho — the first official to resign over the inferno.
Wang Fuk residents and other critics have in recent months expressed anger at a perceived lack of government accountability.
The Hong Kong government has set up an independent team to investigate which officials should be held accountable and to outline disciplinary actions.

Lee, whose five-year term ends next June, did not directly respond to press questions over whether he would seek another term, saying “implementing the reforms is the goal” rather than personal matters.

Lee said Hong Kong’s Chief Secretary Eric Chan will now head a steering committee to oversee reforms advocated in the report, which will include laws to criminalise bid rigging across the construction industry with fines of up to HK$10 million and 10 years’ imprisonment.
The committee report said contractor Prestige Construction & Engineering Co Ltd and project consultant Will Power Architects Co Ltd should bear primary responsibility.

At least 25 criminal charges related to the Wang Fuk Court fire have been made against Prestige, Will Power and seven individuals, including manslaughter, conspiracy to defraud, money laundering and tax evasion.
But the report also went further, outlining widespread unlawful and dubious construction practices as a “corrupt eco-system.”
The rigging of bids in the industry involved many different parties, some linked to triad organized crime gangs, it said.

The committee held 30 hearings this year with 80 witnesses, including residents, property management and renovation personnel, engineering and fire experts, government officials and regulators. It evaluated more than one million files and submissions as it investigated the cause of the fire and reviewed oversight of building renovations.

Before the report’s release, critics had said the committee lacked the statutory powers of a full public inquiry, which could potentially limit its ability to establish the full facts and accountability.

Some groups in the Asian business hub have called for more transparency and accountability, amid warnings from authorities that any attempts to politicise the disaster would be severely punished. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Survey period didn't cover hearings on alleged unexplained wealth, says prosecutor
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel has no reason to be demoralized amid the latest Social Weather Stations (SWS) survey showing that 35% of Filipinos are dissatisfied with the prosecution of the impeachment…

blocks.text: Published October 29, 2026 8:56pm

The House prosecution panel has no reason to be demoralized amid the latest Social Weather Stations (SWS) survey showing that 35% of Filipinos are dissatisfied with the prosecution of the impeachment case against Vice President Sara Duterte, House prosecution panel spokesperson Zia Adiong of Lanao del Sur said Thursday.

Adiong said that the said poll was conducted last Septmber 21 to 27, a period that did not cover the prosecution’s presentation of evidence of the Vice President’s financial records which seeks to prove Article 2 or the Vice President’s alleged accumulation of unexplained wealth due to undeclared assets and non-divestment in businesses as mandated by the Constitution.

“The survey is not supposed to demoralize the prosecution because our track is based on a constitutional premise: Accountability. We all saw how the trial went. The Vice President was given due process to explain herself,” Adiong said in a press conference.

“The prosecution’s focus is really to hold the Vice President to account based on constitutional duty. The survey is not for us and may speak of different things. It cannot be automatically translated into the prosecution doing not the right thing,” he added.

The impeachment case against the Vice President rests only on one: Article 2 which alleges unexplained wealth due to non-declaration of assets in the SALN and non-divestment of businesses despite Constitutional prohibition.

The House prosecution panel dropped three charges of impeachment including: Article 1 on confidential fund, Article 3 on bribery and Article 4 on grave threat to President Ferdinand Marcos, Jr. and his family after lawyer and certified public accountant Alex Cabrera testified that the Vice President and her husband said recorded P817 million unexplained wealth at the minimum and P1.5 billion at the maximum.

Cabrera made the conclusion after reviewing the financial records of the Vice President and her husband which include: SALNs, bank transaction and bank deposit records, insurance payment records, income tax returns and corporate records of the busines interests of the Duterte-Carpio couple.
“What drives us to move forward is the constitutional duty of the prosecution to hold the Vice President to account,” Adiong said.
Likewise, Adiong said the same survey showing that 78% of respondents believes it is important for the Vice President to testify personally to address the allegations against her.
“There is a high percentage of the public who wants the Vice President to explain, and that speaks a lot on the a public clamor for an explanation directly from the Vice President,” Adiong said.
“That speaks about their belief that an irregularity happened and that is the most important thing that we need to focus on,” he added. —NB, GMA News

articles.title: Volkswagen logs Q3 operating loss of €5.86 billion on Porsche writedown
articles.summary: The Volkswagen Group has filed its worst quarterly performance since the height of the "Dieselgate" scandal in 2015. Share prices climbed in response, however, perhaps because the bad news was so…

image.caption: The VW group has been selling roughly 10% fewer units worldwide, but at slightly higher average prices compared to last year [FILE: March 7, 2025]Image: Julian Stratenschulte/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: The Volkswagen Group on Thursday posted its worst quarterly numbers in more than a decade.

The company reported an operating loss of €5.86 billion (roughly $6.53 billion) during July, August and September. One-off costs, not least a massive writedown in its stake in struggling sister company Porsche, explained the vast bulk of the losses.
The world's second-largest carmaker is battling mounting competition from and falling demand in the core Chinese market.
It is pursuing a major restructuring and downsizing program, trying to bolster falling profit margins, and executives said the difficulties highlighted the urgency of this process.
"The nine-month results make one thing clear: We cannot afford to lose any time. We must act quickly and decisively," chief financial officer Arno Antlitz said in a video statement.

blocks.caption: During his state visit to core auto market China this week, German Presidnet Frank-Walter Steinmeier went to the Volkswagen China LabImage: Frank Ossenbrink/IMAGO

blocks.text: What were the main takeaways from VW's Q3 figures?

The results were the latest reminder of the pressure on VW — and the wider German and Western automotive industry — to react to increasing competition in China, high costs and practical difficulties moving towards electric car production, and unpredictable and rising tariff burdens, thanks in no small part to US President Donald Trump.
Here are some of the key Q3 figures:

items: An operating loss of €5.86 billion, compared to €1.3 billion in same quarter last year
It's the company's worst single quarterly loss since the height of the "Dieselgate" emissions scandal in 2015
Sales revenue dipped 6.3% year-on-year, to €75.3 billion
Deliveries to customers, unit sales, and unit production numbers all dipped by roughly 15% as the company starts to reduce production levels, trying to adjust to falling demand

blocks.text: And here are some of the key year-to-date 9-month figures:

items: Sales revenue of €233.4 billion was broadly comparable to 2025's figure of €238.7 billion
But vehicle unit sales, at 5.9 million, are 11% lower than 6.6 million last year — meaning the group is selling fewer cars, at higher prices
The company's order intake for new cars rose 4% year-on-year, and by 39% for battery electric vehicles (BEVs)
Operating profit lies at just €0.1 billion, compared with €5.4 billion a year ago
But VW said 'special items' amounting to €8.7 billion primarily explain this massive dip
Non-cash writedowns on Porsche assets worth €6.4 billion were the largest portion of this

blocks.text: Can Volkswagen stage an automotive comeback?
How did investors respond?

VW shares were already at their lowest levels in well over 10 years prior to Thursday's announcements, after months of difficult headlines and the ongoing plans to shed tens of thousands of jobs and reduce production capacities.
Perhaps as a result of this, the stock dipped briefly as markets opened and the news was published, but then started to rally as the day progressed.
By midday in Frankfurt, VW shares had climbed by 2% compared to their prices at the start of trading on the DAX.
Volkswagen crisis: Emden plant closure impacts whole region
What are VW's downsizing plans?

CEO Oliver Blume plans to shed around 100,000 jobs across the group, which includes the Audi and Porsche brands, in the coming years though a combination of layoffs and not replacing departing or retiring personnel.

Multiple factors are contributing to this. They include increased competition from Chinese manufacturers, falling revenues in China, changeable US auto tariffs under President Donald Trump, different staffing requirements when manufacturing electric cars and difficulties moving towards making and selling more electric cars at the pace once designated by political leaders.
Up to four plants in Germany could face closure as part of the plan, which has met with considerable union resistance and could lead to strikes starting next year.
CFO Antlitz said the figures showed the urgency underlying these plans, saying the company needed to increase its profit margins by 2030 to solidify its finances.
Antlitz said the operating return on sales was only 3.8% in the first nine months of the year, even before the one-off writedowns hitting the bottom line.
"That is not enough in the long term," he said.
As part of its restructuring program, the VW Group aims to restore an operating profit margin of between 8-10% by 2030.
This year, amid one-off costs now totaling in the region of €10 billion, it expects a profit margin of no more than 1%, compared to prior forecasts in the region of 5%.
Germany under pressure

articles.title: Russian drone attack on Ukrainian train station kills at least 13, officials say
articles.summary: Dnipro regional head Oleksandr Hanzha said at least 10 others were wounded in the attack, including an 11-year-old boy.

blocks.text: Thirteen people have been killed after a Russian jet-powered drone hit a crowded platform at Dnipro railway station in the country's north, Ukrainian officials have said.
Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha said at least 10 others were wounded in the attack, including an 11-year-old boy.
According to the Ukrainian railway operator, Ukrzaliznytsia, a train headed for Zaporizhzhia was at one of the platforms in Dnipro when the drone hit.
Moscow has repeatedly targeted Ukraine's large railway network but it denies deliberately targeting civilians.

Elsewhere in Ukraine, two girls aged 15 were killed in a Russian missile attack on the centre of Chernihiv city, in the north of the country, regional head Vyacheslav Chaus said. At least 11 others, including more children, were injured, he added.
In Dnipro, an elevated threat level was announced ahead of Thursday's strike, according to Ukraine Railways head Oleksandr Pertsovsky.
"But unfortunately there were still a large number of people on the platform," he said.
Dnipro Mayor Borys Filatov said the incident was a tragedy, adding that a drone hit a civilian electric train.
Pictures from the Ukrainian rescue services show a large hole ripped in a platform strewn with blurred-out bodies, near a blast-damaged train with smashed windows.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said "the Russians used a drone to attack a platform where a regular commuter train and a regular passenger train were standing."

He called for further US, European and G7 sanctions on Russia following the incident and repeated his criticism of a controversial deal struck earlier this month between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, which eased some sanctions on Russia, allowing the US to import Russian diesel.

The strikes came during efforts to uphold a fragile local ceasefire in the besieged city of Oleshky - which has been under Russian occupation since 2022 and where residents have been trapped without food, water, medicine and electricity.

Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said on Telegram the truce was holding into a third day, and he had "set out with the Ukrainian delegation towards Oleshky" through Belarus and Russia.

Meanwhile, the Kremlin has condemned Ukrainian drone attacks on Moscow whilst the city hosts the Russia-Africa Summit, the Tass news agency has reported. The summit is a two-day event attended by African leaders and government delegations from 48 countries.
The mayor of Moscow said 613 Ukrainian drones were launched overnight towards the region, most of which were shot down during their flight.
Russia's defence ministry has always denied targeting Ukrainian civilians and says its attacks on railways target the infrastructure used to transport military personnel and equipment.
However, the dangers to passengers are very real. Attacks on Ukraine's rolling stock and stations have risen sharply.

Of the 521 locomotives hit since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion, almost 60% have been his this year, according to statistics released by Ukrzaliznytsia supplied to AFP news agency. Overall attacks on railway facilities have risen from 1,206 in 2025 to 1,700 so far this year.
There appears to have been a wider assault on Ukraine's infrastructure in recent weeks, with two bridges attacked in Kyiv, and a metro train hit during one of the strikes.
